motion: Does the historical evidence of suffering justify confidence in the sincerity of all the original resurrection witnesses?

bridges.description: Connect continued public commitment under expected suffering to the probability of sincere resurrection belief.
Combine unequal martyrdom evidence, collective testimony, and persecution patterns without requiring identical evidence for every witness.
Treat continued public association with a threatened movement as relevant even without individual preaching or a final recantation chance.
Test whether evidence about limited leaders justifies confidence about all original witnesses.
Separate death or persecution from proof that abandonment of the resurrection claim could have prevented it.
Require evidence before treating a flexible title or collective narrative as proof that each original witness preached and remained exposed.
